content.user_title: Estimate Agile Tasks With Story Points
content.value_statement: Teams need consistent estimates for sprint planning and roadmaps. This skill guides story points, planning poker, sizing, risks, and task breakdowns.
actual_capabilities: Maps task complexity to Fibonacci story point ranges.
Explains a planning poker workflow for team consensus.
Converts rough work into t-shirt size estimates.
Adds buffers for risk and uncertainty.
Provides an estimation document template with risks and dependencies.
limitations: Requires clear task details, acceptance criteria, and dependencies.
Does not inspect repositories or project history automatically.
Estimates depend on each team's velocity and delivery context.
Time ranges are planning aids, not delivery commitments.

use_cases.title: Plan a sprint backlog
use_cases.description: Estimate candidate stories, compare effort, and choose a realistic sprint scope.

use_cases.title: Shape a product roadmap
use_cases.description: Turn feature ideas into rough sizes before sequencing quarterly work.

use_cases.title: Review engineering risk
use_cases.description: Adjust estimates for unknowns, dependencies, integration work, and testing needs.

prompt_templates.title: Estimate a single task
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner estimation for a clear backlog item.
prompt_templates.prompt: Estimate this task with story points, t-shirt size, time range, risks, dependencies, and assumptions: [task details].

prompt_templates.title: Prepare planning poker notes
prompt_templates.prompt: Create planning poker notes for this story. Include questions, likely estimate range, risk factors, and reasons for high or low votes: [story].

prompt_templates.title: Split a large epic
prompt_templates.scenario: Backlog refinement for work that exceeds 13 points.
prompt_templates.prompt: Break this epic into smaller estimable stories. For each story, include acceptance criteria, estimate, dependencies, and open questions: [epic].

prompt_templates.title: Calibrate a roadmap estimate
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning using team context and historical velocity.
prompt_templates.prompt: Using this team velocity and backlog, estimate delivery ranges. Show confidence, sequencing risks, dependencies, and where estimates need discovery: [context].

output_examples.input: Task: Add profile photo upload with size validation and existing cloud storage.
output_examples.output: Estimate: 5 story points, medium size, and 1-2 days. Main risks are file validation, image processing, and permission checks.

output_examples.input: Epic: Add subscription payments for web and mobile users.
output_examples.output: Recommendation: split the epic. Create separate stories for checkout, account status, webhook handling, refunds, mobile purchase flow, and testing.

output_examples.input: Roadmap item: Build an admin analytics dashboard with unknown reporting requirements.
output_examples.output: Estimate: high uncertainty. Run discovery first, define required metrics, then estimate charts, export needs, permissions, and performance work separately.

best_practices: Provide acceptance criteria before asking for an estimate.
Compare each task with similar completed work.
Separate high-risk unknowns into discovery tasks.
anti_patterns: Do not treat estimates as promises from individuals.
Do not estimate large epics without splitting them first.
Do not ignore team velocity, dependencies, or technical risk.

faq.question: Can this skill estimate both points and time?
faq.answer: Yes. It can provide story points, t-shirt sizes, and rough time ranges when enough context is available.

faq.question: Does it replace team planning poker?
faq.answer: No. It helps prepare discussion, but final estimates should come from team consensus.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the task goal, acceptance criteria, dependencies, risks, and any similar past work.

faq.question: Can it estimate large epics?
faq.answer: It can identify large epics and suggest smaller stories before assigning final estimates.

faq.question: Does it use project history automatically?
faq.answer: No. You need to provide velocity, past estimates, or delivery history if you want calibration.
